In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ACVRL1 is associated with more severe disease than ENG.
the genetic variants in ENG gene are associated with a higher risk of pulmonary and cerebral APMs, and the ACVRL1 genetic variants are associated with a more severe liver disease.
ACVRL1 mutation carriers have more frequent and severe liver and hematological manifestations, while ENG mutation carriers have more severe vascular manifestations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RiHHT registry is an important tool for genetic counseling of HHT patients and their relatives.
ACVRL1 mutation carriers have a more severe phenotype than ENG mutation carriers.
ACVRL1 is more frequent in Spain and is related to a more severe disease, while ENG variants are related to a milder disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical presentation and severity of HHT is highly variable and that the genetic background may play an important role.
genetic testing in HHT patients is essential in clinical practice to provide accurate diagnosis and genetic counseling.
the genetic test is useful to identify patients with HHT and to guide the follow-up and management of the disease.
